title: Jobs, CronJobs, DaemonSets, StatefulSets
summary: Not everything is a stateless web server: pick the controller that fits.

steps.title: Four more controllers
body: | **Job** | running pods until N complete successfully | DB migration, batch import, report |
| **CronJob** | creating Jobs on a schedule (`"0 2 * * *"`) | nightly backup, cleanup |
| **DaemonSet** | exactly one pod on every (matching) node | log collector, node monitoring, CNI agent |
| **StatefulSet** | pods with **stable names and their own disks**, started in order | databases, Kafka, ZooKeeper, Elasticsearch |

A Job's pod should exit 0 when done; it then shows `Completed`. On failure the Job retries up to `backoffLimit` (default 6). Set `restartPolicy: Never` or `OnFailure` in a Job's pod template; `Always` is for long-running services.
CronJob schedules use the five cron fields `minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week`, in the controller's time zone unless you set `timeZone`.

items: a stateless REST API with 5 replicas
Fluent Bit log shipper on every node
PostgreSQL primary with its own disk
run database migrations once per release
a React front end served by nginx

steps.title: Why StatefulSets exist
body: A Deployment's pods are interchangeable: random names (`web-7d9f-2xkqp`), shared or no storage, started all at once. A database cluster needs the opposite:
- **Stable identity**: `db-0` is always `db-0`, even after rescheduling, so replicas can say "db-0 is the primary".
- **Stable storage**: each pod gets its own PersistentVolumeClaim from `volumeClaimTemplates`, which follows it to any node and is **not** deleted when you scale down.
- **Order**: pods start 0, 1, 2 (each Ready before the next) and stop in reverse, 2, 1, 0.
> **Tip:** Running a database in Kubernetes is possible, but a managed database (Azure Database, RDS, Cloud SQL) is usually less work. Choose a StatefulSet when you need to run it yourself.

steps.prompt: You scale StatefulSet `db` from 3 replicas to 1. What happens to the volumes?
options: Pods `db-2` then `db-1` are deleted; their PVCs `data-db-2` and `data-db-1` are kept so the data is there if you scale back up
steps.explain: Kubernetes refuses to guess that you are done with data. You delete leftover PVCs yourself (newer clusters can set `persistentVolumeClaimRetentionPolicy`).

steps.prompt: Match each pod name to the controller that most likely created it.
pairs: CronJob (Job named after the scheduled time)
DaemonSet (one random suffix, one per node)

steps.prompt: A migration Job keeps failing and you see six pods named `migrate-xxxxx` in `Error`. Why did it stop at six?
options: The Job's `backoffLimit` (default 6) was reached and the Job is marked failed
The cluster only allows six pods per Job
CronJobs run six times a day
steps.explain: Check `kubectl logs job/migrate` (or one of the pods) for the cause. `kubectl describe job migrate` shows `BackoffLimitExceeded`.

steps.prompt: StatefulSet scale-down order. What does this print?
code: for (int i = from - 1; i >= to; i--)
steps.explain: Highest ordinal first. Scaling up creates `db-2`, `db-3` again in ascending order and reattaches their old PVCs.

steps.title: Scale a StatefulSet
prompt: Write `List<string> Scale(string name, int from, int to)` returning the actions a StatefulSet controller takes, one pod at a time:

- scale up: `"create name-i"` for each new ordinal in **ascending** order, plus `"create pvc data-name-i"` **before** each pod, but only if that ordinal never existed before (in this exercise, ordinals below `from` existed; ordinals at or above `from` never did)
- scale down: `"delete name-i"` in **descending** order (PVCs are kept, so no PVC actions)
`Scale("db", 1, 3)` returns `["create pvc data-db-1", "create db-1", "create pvc data-db-2", "create db-2"]`.
starter: List<string> Scale(string name, int from, int to)
solution: List<string> Scale(string name, int from, int to)
for (int i = from; i < to; i++)
for (int i = from - 1; i >= to; i--)
template: Dojo.Eq("Scale(\"db\", 1, 3)", new List<string> { "create pvc data-db-1", "create db-1", "create pvc data-db-2", "create db-2" }, Scale("db", 1, 3));
Dojo.Eq("Scale(\"kafka\", 3, 1)", new List<string> { "delete kafka-2", "delete kafka-1" }, Scale("kafka", 3, 1));
Dojo.Eq("Scale(\"zk\", 0, 1)", new List<string> { "create pvc data-zk-0", "create zk-0" }, Scale("zk", 0, 1));
hints: Two loops: one counting up from `from` to `to - 1`, one counting down from `from - 1` to `to`.
Only one of the loops runs for any given call.
